newsitem.title: UK: Signet to restructure capital, convert shares.
newsitem.headline: Signet to restructure capital, convert shares.

text.p: UK jewellery retailer Signet Plc said on Wednesday it plans to restructure its share capital by converting all classes of preference shares into around 1.38 billion new ordinary shares.

The capital reorganisation of the jeweller, formerly Ratners, will include the cancellation of preference shareholders accumulated dividend arrears and accruals, amounting to 164.5 million stg ($272.2 million) as at May 15. The group also announced an 80 percent increase in profits for the year to February 1 1997 to 45.1 million stg.

Signet, which has not been paying dividends for several years, said the elimination of the accumulated deficit on its profit and loss account of 199.0 million stg, would give it the ability to pay dividends out of future profits, subject to court approval.
The group will hold a shareholder meeting on June 26 for investors to vote on the restructuring.
Signet chairman James McAdam said the improvement in profits had paved the way for the proposed capital reorganisation.
"This improved performance provides the right platform to move forward with the proposed capital reorganisation which we believe is in the best interests of the company and its shareholders."
Signet's shares were unchanged at 36.5 pence.
